title: SSE stream can yield an older delta after a newer state snapshot (biased select over two channels)
outcome: Broadcast state and delta events reach each client on one channel in the order they were broadcast, so among broadcast events a delta is never delivered after a snapshot of a later revision. The initial and lag-recovery snapshots are catch-up points built for one client: retained broadcast events of a lower revision may follow them and are not suppressed for that revision, and the client handles them under its own revision, identity and body-sequence rules. A client that cannot keep up is resynchronised to its recoverable state; notification-only events already lost to overflow are not replayed.
acceptance: A client that cannot keep up with the stream is resynchronised with a full snapshot and is never left with a gap between the events it received; a test shows a lagging receiver.

Broadcast state and delta events yielded from one channel retain their broadcast order: among those broadcast events a delta of revision N is never yielded after a state event of a revision above N; a test at the stream layer fails without the fix and passes with it. The initial snapshot and a lag-recovery snapshot are built for one client outside that order: retained broadcast events of a lower revision may follow them and are not suppressed merely because of that revision. Tests show that such retained events, including a notification-only delta, are yielded; the client prevents stale metadata rollback under its revision and identity rules, processes body deltas under their per-session sequence and epoch rules rather than discarding them solely for an older global revision, and still handles an applicable notice.
The feature documentation of the state broadcast states the ordering guarantee and what a lagging client gets.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.

completion.summary: The SSE catch-up contract after a snapshot is pinned by stream-layer and client tests, and the state-broadcast docs are narrowed.
